extracted.intended_audience: U.S. Department of Education officials; K-12 school administrators, Title IX coordinators, and educators
extracted.subtask_description: Policy testimony recommending how ED should improve enforcement of Title IX in K-12 schools, including required policies, training, definitions of harassment, interim guidance, use of restorative justice, and protections for LGBTQ students and reporters. Focused on actionable regulatory and school-level practices to prevent and address sexual harassment and discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require written sexual harassment policies and awareness measures
rubrics_metrics.description: ED should require schools to issue sexual harassment policies, provide educators and staff with sexual harassment training, and utilize anonymous surveys about sexual harassment and school climate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek input of educators, students, families, and diverse community members when developing policies, trainings, and surveys. Require clear statements about the rights of students and educators to a school environment free from sexual harassment and ensure awareness by training educators on the policy, posting the policy in conspicuous locations, making it accessible on the school's website, training students during orientation, and including it in student materials (e.g., student handbook).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive, trauma-informed sexual harassment training
rubrics_metrics.description: Any sexual harassment training schools offer must go beyond just defining prohibited conduct. The training should be comprehensive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training should help students and educators understand what behavior constitutes sexual harassment, the harms of sexual harassment, the school's procedures for reporting, options for students and educators who experience harassment, and information about supportive services for targets. Trainings should be trauma-informed and account for the unique experiences, harms, and needs of students of color, students with disabilities, and LGBTQ students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct school climate and harassment surveys with demographic data
rubrics_metrics.description: Schools and districts should conduct surveys about sexual harassment and school climate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surveys may uncover gaps in reporting and misunderstandings about reporting procedures, and provide information about whether students and staff feel protected and supported. Include demographic information (race, gender, LGBTQ status, special education status) to identify and respond to disproportionate sexual harassment experienced by particular groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide comprehensive, age-appropriate sexual health education
rubrics_metrics.description: ED should encourage schools to offer comprehensive, age-appropriate sexual health education courses in all K-12 schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curricula should cover healthy relationships, sexual decision making and self-discipline, refusal skills and personal boundaries, consent, dating and sexual violence prevention, and information about sexual orientation and gender identity. Evidence shows such education reduces likelihood of experiencing or engaging in sexual violence and meets student demand for covering emotional aspects of romantic relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure qualified, independent, visible Title IX coordinators
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX coordinators must be adequately trained, visible and accessible, have independence and authority, be free of conflicts of interest, have full-time roles with full-time resources, and maintain institutional knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstate the 2015 Dear Colleague Letter guidance recommending a Title IX Coordinator at every institution. Knowledgeable, well-trained coordinators serve as necessary local points of contact for educators navigating rights and responsibilities around sexual harassment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use federal funds to provide trauma-informed student supports
rubrics_metrics.description: ED should advise schools on how to use American Rescue Plan funds and other federal grants to support students who have experienced sexual violence, including sexual harassment and assault.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As districts add counselors, social workers, and nurses, ensure support for students who experienced sexual violence is explicitly included in mental health supports. ED should consider grant or innovation programs to assist proactive districts addressing student trauma.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amend actionable sexual harassment definition to a broader, uniform standard
rubrics_metrics.description: ED must amend the 2020 regulation's narrowed definition ("so severe, pervasive, and objectively offensive") to a broader standard and apply a single, consistent standard for unwelcome conduct across protected categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restore a definition consistent with prior guidance (e.g., 'unwelcome conduct of a sexual nature') and ensure parity with protections for harassment based on race and other traits. Include sex-based harassment such as sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, transgender status, sex stereotypes, sex characteristics, parental status, pregnancy, childbirth, termination of pregnancy, and related conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide recourse for off-campus and online harassment
rubrics_metrics.description: A new rule must include recourse for students who suffer off-campus harassment that effectively denies them access to or the benefit of education programs or activities, particularly online/cyberbullying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that off-campus conduct, including online harassment among classmates, can impact K-12 students' access to education. ED should specifically address sexual harassment in online forums that affect students' equal access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect reporters and survivors from retaliation and disciplinary consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: ED must ensure students who report sexual harassment or assault do not suffer additional consequences as a result of reporting and should prohibit schools from disciplining students for conduct disclosed in their complaints or conduct resulting from the harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: schools must not punish students for substance use violations when disclosed as occurring before an assault; must not discipline students for unexcused absences when avoiding classes with their harasser. ED should also ensure students who transferred or dropped out due to harassment still have access to relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue interim guidance on addressing non-actionable harmful conduct and prevention
rubrics_metrics.description: Until rulemaking, ED must provide guidance regarding forms of harassment outside the scope of the 2020 regulation and clear standards for addressing harmful conduct before it becomes actionable under the current rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide tools and examples for addressing online harassment, and detailed guidance on developing codes of conduct and policies that prohibit and address harassing behavior that may not meet the narrow 2020 standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on informal resolution and restorative justice practices
rubrics_metrics.description: ED should provide guidance on when recipients can address sexual harassment under less formal procedures than a full Title IX investigation and what informal procedures are acceptable, including restorative justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss ways schools may use restorative justice practices, emphasize that restorative justice is a comprehensive cultural transformation aligned with values of respect, dignity, mutual concern, justice and equity, and belief in each person's worth. Offer models and examples (e.g., Oakland Unified School District, NEA/Denver Public Schools guide) and outline how restorative practices integrate with professional development, trauma-informed practices, positive behavioral supports, family inclusion, and peer programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define sex discrimination to include sexual orientation and gender identity and enumerate prohibited acts
rubrics_metrics.description: ED must issue detailed guidance clarifying that 'on the basis of sex' includes discrimination based on gender identity, gender expression, transgender status, sexual orientation, sex stereotypes, and sex characteristics, and must clarify concrete examples of discriminatory or harassing acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify that prohibited acts include excluding students from activities because of sexual orientation or transgender status; misgendering; refusing to use a chosen name; disclosing a student's transgender/nonbinary status without consent; prohibiting participation in sex-segregated activities matching gender identity; denying access to restrooms/locker rooms consistent with gender identity; imposing dress codes that bar gender-consistent clothing; and bullying based on actual or perceived sexual orientation/gender identity or that of associates. Encourage schools to adopt gender-affirming policies, create Gender & Sexualities Alliances (GSAs), adopt gender-neutral dress codes, incorporate LGBTQ history into curricula, and ensure sexual health education is inclusive of LGBTQ concerns.
